Preserve original body proportions and armor material/colors. No red V mask, no broad orange flame feathers, no short broad sword, no segmented pants substituted for the long dark skirt, no new equipment. Original black/gold boots and lower legs are visible below/between the existing long skirt panels. The skirt is not a solid cone: its existing hanging panels swing naturally with the walking legs, retaining their original long lengths and gold edges. Do not shorten or delete the skirt to show legs, do not invent trousers or gaps in the original armor.

DIRECTION: every one of the six figures walks SOUTH, straight TOWARD THE VIEWER / SCREEN DOWN. Fixed elevated isometric camera, front of the pale face, FRONT chest and waist visible all six phases, both hip sides and both lower legs shown. Do not rotate to east/west, do not turn the head sideways or away, do not mirror the whole model to get opposite steps. The SAME anatomical right leg remains on IMAGE LEFT in all poses; SAME anatomical left leg remains IMAGE RIGHT. The same right-hand long weapon stays IMAGE LEFT in all six; armor details, spine attachments and asymmetrical weapon hand never swap sides.

CRUCIAL REQUIREMENT: show a real alternating-leg walk rather than six variations of the same right-leading stance. Across the cycle the two identifiable boots must VISIBLY EXCHANGE front/back DEPTH positions. When a foot steps forward toward the viewer it is LOWER on the screen and slightly larger/foreshortened; the trailing foot is HIGHER on screen. Make forward/trailing depth differences clear enough to verify at game scale. The original long skirt panels naturally swing apart over the moving boots to reveal the actual alternating knee/ankle arrangement. Use a moderate deliberate grounded walk, NO run or flight. Weight alternates supported hips and knees, passing foot lifts, trailing toe pushes off. Genuine distinct articulated leg positions, not rigidly translated or bobbed copies.

Exactly six phases in LEFT-TO-RIGHT, TOP-TO-BOTTOM order:
0 RIGHT CONTACT: anatomical RIGHT leg at IMAGE LEFT reaches FORWARD toward viewer/screen bottom, clearly LOWER than the left boot. Right heel contacts; LEFT leg at IMAGE RIGHT trails BACK/higher on screen with toe pushing. Pelvis and weight lead on the right, torso subtly counterrotates, face stays front SOUTH.
1 RIGHT SUPPORT / LEFT PASSING: right leg IMAGE LEFT bears weight nearly under right hip; LEFT knee/boot IMAGE RIGHT lifts and passes forward from the rear. Left boot temporarily higher and off ground, right foot clearly supports. Existing dark skirt panels swing with these actual two knees.
2 LEFT ARRIVING / RIGHT PUSH: LEFT leg at IMAGE RIGHT reaches FORWARD toward the viewer and becomes LOWER than the right boot; RIGHT leg IMAGE LEFT is now behind/higher with toe pushing off. This MUST be the opposite depth order from phase0.
3 LEFT CONTACT: anatomical LEFT leg at IMAGE RIGHT is clearly FORWARD/LOWER and supports its heel; RIGHT leg IMAGE LEFT is BACK/HIGHER with trailing toe. This is the true opposite-leg counterpart of phase0, with the SAME asymmetrical right-hand weapon and same frontal face, never a mirrored whole sprite.
4 LEFT SUPPORT / RIGHT PASSING: left leg IMAGE RIGHT supports nearly under left hip; RIGHT knee/boot IMAGE LEFT lifts and passes forward from rear. Right boot temporarily higher/off ground, left clearly supports. Weight/body counterrotation differs from phase1 while equipment stays on correct side.
5 RIGHT ARRIVING / LEFT PUSH: RIGHT leg at IMAGE LEFT reaches forward/LOWER again, LEFT leg IMAGE RIGHT is back/higher pushing from the toe, approaching phase0 smoothly. The six-phase loop should continue naturally into right contact.

Animate restrained opposite arm/shoulder response without swapping the original weapon hand, tiny body weight bob, and believable lag of the long pale hair and existing gold-trim dark skirt. Narrow hard golden back spines remain attached, consistent in count/construction, with very small torso-linked sway only. Keep both boots and the low skirt hem unobstructed by the long weapon; the weapon may hang to the viewer-left OUTSIDE the stride rather than crossing the feet.
